596: static uint32_t ack_header_reason(
597:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
598:   const struct active_transaction *active)
599: {
600:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
601:   uint32_t reason = 0;
602: 
603:   if (!active->busy)
604:     {
605:       return 1u;
606:     }
607: 
608:   if (control != BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
609:     {
610:       reason |= 2u;
611:     }
612:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) !=
613:       bk7258_mb_header_channel(&active->message))
614:     {
615:       reason |= 4u;
616:     }
617:   if (bk7258_mb_header_seq(message) !=
618:       bk7258_mb_header_seq(&active->message))
619:     {
620:       reason |= 8u;
621:     }
622:   if (bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) !=
623:       bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&active->message))
624:     {
625:       reason |= 16u;
626:     }
627: 
628:   return reason;
629: }

665: 
666: 
667:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
668:       !valid_uart_ack(message))
669:     {
670:       /* Keep active stable.  A malformed ACK is not an ownership proof. */
671: 
672:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
673:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 32u;
674:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
675:       return;
676:     }
677: 
678:   if ((bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & ~BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0)
679:     {
680:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
681:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 64u;
682:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
683:       return;
684:     }
685: 
686:   result = (bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0 ?
687:            -EREMOTEIO : OK;
688: 
689:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
690:       result == OK && (message->payload_address & 2u) != 0)
691:     {
692:       result = -EREMOTEIO;
693:     }
694: 
695:   replay = active == &epoch->probe && epoch->replay;
696:   release_acks_before(replay ? epoch->first_probe_order : active->order);
697:   if (replay)
698:     {
699:       unsigned int replay_index = g_recovery_index;
700:       unsigned int i;
701: 
702:       /* This ACK may be a late ACK for the original copy.  It proves every
703:        * older epoch was copied, but not that the new replay envelope was
704:        * copied.  Preserve the replay epoch, free only older epochs, and use
705:        * one of them for a fresh-sequence confirmation probe.
706:        */
707: 
708:       complete_transaction(active, message, -EAGAIN);
709:       g_active.quarantine = false;
710:       for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
711:         {
712:           if (i != replay_index)
713:             {
714:               memset(&g_recovery[i], 0, sizeof(g_recovery[i]));
715:             }
716:         }
717: 
718:       select_recovery_epoch();
719:       (void)dispatch_locked();
720:       return;
721:     }
722: 
723:   complete_transaction(active, message, result);
724: 
725:   if (active == &epoch->probe)
726:     {
727:       if (result == OK && (message->flags & 2u) == 0)
728:         {
729:           release_recovery_slots();
730:           g_recovery_index = 0;
731:           g_probe_attempts = 0;
732:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_READY);
733:         }
734:       else if (result == -EREMOTEIO &&
735:                g_probe_attempts < MB_PROBE_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
736:         {
737:           /* CP may not have opened MB_UART0 yet.  The matched ACK proves
738:            * that this probe slot is no longer referenced by its FIFO.
739:            */
740:         }
741:       else
742:         {
743:           g_stats.probe_fail++;
744:           epoch->probe.quarantine = result == -ETIMEDOUT;
745:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN);
746:         }
747:     }
748: 
749:   else if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
750:            result < 0)
751:     {
752:       begin_abort(result);
753:     }
754: 
755:   (void)dispatch_locked();
756: }

758: static int handle_command(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
759: {
760:   struct ack_slot *slot;
761:   unsigned int rx_index;
762:   uint8_t channel = bk7258_mb_header_channel(message);
763:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
764:   uint8_t ack_flags = 0;
765:   uint8_t state = 0;
766:   int ret = -ENOSYS;
767: 
768:   g_stats.last_command_header = message->header;
769: 
770:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) == 0)
771:     {
772:       slot = alloc_ack_slot();
773:       if (slot == NULL)
774:         {
775:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
776:           return -EAGAIN;
777:         }
778:     }
779:   else
780:     {
781:       slot = NULL;
782:     }
783: 
784:   if ((control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0 ||
785:       bk7258_mb_header_state(message) != 0 ||
786:       (channel & 0xf0u) != 0x40u)
787:     {
788:       g_stats.bad_header++;
789:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
790:     }
791:   else if ((rx_index = rx_channel_index(channel)) < MB_RX_CHANNEL_COUNT &&
792:            g_rx_callbacks[rx_index] != NULL)
793:     {
794:       ret = g_rx_callbacks[rx_index](message, &ack_flags,
795:                                       g_rx_args[rx_index]);
796:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
797:         {
798:           if (slot != NULL)
799:             {
800:               slot->state = ACK_SLOT_FREE;
801:             }
802: 
803:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
804:           return -EAGAIN;
805:         }
806:       else if (ret < 0)
807:         {
808:           state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
809:         }
810:     }
811:   else if (channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_PWC_RX && g_pwc_rx != NULL)
812:     {
813:       ret = g_pwc_rx(message);
814:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
815:         {
816:           if (slot != NULL)
817:             {
818:               slot->state = ACK_SLOT_FREE;
819:             }
820: 
821:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
822:           return -EAGAIN;
823:         }
824:       else if (ret < 0)
825:         {
826:           state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
827:         }
828:     }
829:   else if (channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_SARADC_RX &&
830:            (bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) == 0u ||
831:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) == 1u) &&
832:            message->payload_address == 1u &&
833:            message->payload_length == 0u && message->flags == 0u &&
834:            message->crc8 == 0u && message->reserved == 0u)
835:     {
836:       /* Match Armino's SARADC operation-notification ABI. */
837:       ack_flags = 2u;
838:       ret = OK;
839:     }
840:   else
841:     {
842:       g_stats.unsupported++;
843:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
844:     }
845: 
846:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) != 0)
847:     {
848:       return OK;
849:     }
850: 
851:   memset(&slot->message, 0, sizeof(slot->message));
852:   slot->message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
853:     bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message), state, BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX,
854:     bk7258_mb_header_seq(message), channel);
855:   slot->message.payload_address = ack_flags;
856: 
857:   if (ack_slots_used() >= MB_ACK_HIGH_WATER)
858:     {
859:       g_probe_requested = true;
860:     }
861: 
862:   (void)dispatch_locked();
863:   return OK;
864: }
865: 
866: static int mailbox_rx(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
867: {
868:   irqstate_t flags;
869:   uint8_t control;
870: 
871:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
872:   g_stats.rx++;
873:   control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
874: 
875:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET) != 0)
876:     {
877:       if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX) == 0 ||
878:           (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) & 0xf0u) != 0x40u ||
879:           (control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0)
880:         {
881:           g_stats.bad_header++;
882:         }
883:       else
884:         {
885:           g_stats.resets++;
886:           g_peer_reset_generation++;
887:           bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred();
888:           begin_abort(-ECONNRESET);
889:         }
890:     }
891:   else if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX) != 0)
892:     {
893:       handle_ack(message);
894:     }
895:   else
896:     {
897:       int ret = handle_command(message);
898: 
899:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
900:         {
901:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
902:           return ret;
903:         }
904:     }
905: 
906:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
907:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
908:   return OK;
909: }

911: static int mailbox_diag_worker(int argc, char **argv)
912: {
913:   enum bk7258_mb_link_state reported = BK7258_MB_LINK_QUIESCING;
914:   int ret;
915: 
916:   (void)argc;
917:   (void)argv;
918:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
919:   if (ret < 0)
920:     {
921:       return -EXDEV;
922:     }
923: 
924:   for (;;)
925:     {
926:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_diag_sem);
927:       irqstate_t flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
928:       enum bk7258_mb_link_state state = g_diag_state;
929:       bk7258_mb_link_callback_t callback = g_link_callback;
930:       void *callback_arg = g_link_arg;
931:       uint32_t timeout = g_stats.timeout;
932:       uint32_t bad_ack = g_stats.bad_ack;
933:       uint8_t epoch = g_recovery_index;
934: 
935:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
936:       if (reported == state)
937:         {
938:           continue;
939:         }
940: 
941:       reported = state;
942:       if (reported != BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING &&
943:           reported != BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
944:         {
945:           syslog(LOG_WARNING,
946:                  "mailbox: link state=%u epoch=%u timeout=%lu bad_ack=%lu\n",
947:                  reported, epoch, (unsigned long)timeout,
948:                  (unsigned long)bad_ack);
949:         }
950: 
951:       if (callback != NULL)
952:         {
953:           callback(reported, callback_arg);
954:         }
955:     }
956: 
957:   return OK;
958: }

960: static int mailbox_tx_worker(int argc, char **argv)
961: {
962:   int ret;
963: 
964:   (void)argc;
965:   (void)argv;
966:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
967:   if (ret < 0)
968:     {
969:       ret = -EXDEV;
970:     }
971: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
972:   else if (!bk7258_smp_secondary_is_ready())
973:     {
974:       ret = -EAGAIN;
975:     }
976: #endif
977:   if (ret < 0)
978:     {
979:       return ret;
980:     }
981: 
982:   for (;;)
983:     {
984:       struct active_transaction *probe;
985:       irqstate_t flags;
986:       bool request_probe;
987: 
988:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_tx_sem, MB_WORK_INTERVAL);
989:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
990: 
991:       probe = busy_probe();
992:       if ((g_active.busy &&
993:            clock_systime_ticks() - g_active.started >= MB_TIMEOUT) ||
994:           (probe != NULL &&
995:            clock_systime_ticks() - probe->started >= MB_TIMEOUT))
996:         {
997:           g_stats.timeout++;
998:           bk7258_boottrace_detail(3,
999:             (g_stats.last_tx_error & 0xffu) |
1000:             ((g_stats.timeout & 0xffu) << 8) |
1001:             ((g_stats.fifo_full & 0xffu) << 16) |
1002:             ((g_stats.ack_overflow & 0xffu) << 24));
1003:           if (probe != NULL)
1004:             {
1005:               probe->quarantine = true;
1006:               complete_transaction(probe, NULL, -ETIMEDOUT);
1007:               g_stats.probe_fail++;
1008:               set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN);
1009:             }
1010:           else
1011:             {
1012:               begin_abort(-ETIMEDOUT);
1013:             }
1014:         }
1015: 
1016:       if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN &&
1017:           clock_systime_ticks() - g_down_since >= MB_DOWN_RETRY)
1018:         {
1019:           select_recovery_epoch();
1020:         }
1021: 
1022:       (void)dispatch_locked();
1023:       if (g_probe_requested && ack_slots_used() < MB_ACK_HIGH_WATER)
1024:         {
1025:           g_probe_requested = false;
1026:         }
1027: 
1028:       request_probe = g_probe_requested &&
1029:                       g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY &&
1030:                       !g_channels[4].queued && !g_active.busy;
1031:       if (request_probe)
1032:         {
1033:           g_probe_requested = false;
1034:         }
1035: 
1036:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1037: 
1038:       if (request_probe)
1039:         {
1040:           bk7258_mb_uart_request_state();
1041:         }
1042:     }
1043: 
1044:   return OK;
1045: }

1075: int bk7258_mailbox_workers_start(void)
1076: {
1077:   cpu_set_t cpuset;
1078:   int ret;
1079: 
1080:   if (!g_initialized)
1081:     {
1082:       return -EAGAIN;
1083:     }
1084: 
1085:   if (g_workers_started)
1086:     {
1087:       return OK;
1088:     }
1089: 
1090:   ret = wait_secondary_scheduler();
1091:   if (ret < 0)
1092:     {
1093:       return ret;
1094:     }
1095: 
1096: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
1097:   /* All physical CP descriptors must originate on logical CPU0.  Pin the
1098:    * creator before activating the workers so their inherited affinity is
1099:    * CPU0-only from their first scheduled instruction. */
1100: 
1101:   CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
1102:   CPU_SET(0, &cpuset);
1103:   ret = sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset);
1104:   if (ret < 0)
1105:     {
1106:       return ret;
1107:     }
1108: #endif
1109: 
1110:   ret = bk7258_timer_start();
1111:   if (ret < 0)
1112:     {
1113:       return ret;
1114:     }
1115: 
1116:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_TIMER_RETURN);
1117: 
1118:   if (!g_tx_worker_created)
1119:     {
1120:       ret = kthread_create("mbox-v2", MB_TX_BOOT_PRIORITY, 2048,
1121:                            mailbox_tx_worker, NULL);
1122:       if (ret < 0)
1123:         {
1124:           return ret;
1125:         }
1126: 
1127:       g_tx_worker_created = true;
1128:       g_tx_worker_pid = ret;
1129:     }
1130: 
1131:   if (!g_diag_worker_created)
1132:     {
1133:       ret = kthread_create("mbox-diag", 80, 1024, mailbox_diag_worker, NULL);
1134:       if (ret < 0)
1135:         {
1136:           return ret;
1137:         }
1138: 
1139:       g_diag_worker_created = true;
1140:     }
1141: 
1142:   g_workers_started = true;
1143:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_TIMER_READY);
1144:   return OK;
1145: }

1184: int bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(uint8_t logical_channel,
1185:                              const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
1186:                              bk7258_mb_tx_complete_t callback, void *arg)
1187: {
1188:   struct logical_channel *channel;
1189:   unsigned int index;
1190:   irqstate_t flags;
1191: 
1192:   if (!g_initialized || !g_physical_started || message == NULL)
1193:     {
1194:       return -EAGAIN;
1195:     }
1196: 
1197:   index = channel_index(logical_channel);
1198:   if (index >= MB_CHANNEL_COUNT)
1199:     {
1200:       return -EINVAL;
1201:     }
1202: 
1203:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1204:   channel = &g_channels[index];
1205: 
1206:   if (channel->queued)
1207:     {
1208:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1209:       return -EBUSY;
1210:     }
1211: 
1212:   if (g_link_state != BK7258_MB_LINK_READY &&
1213:       !(g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING &&
1214:         logical_channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
1215:         bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE))
1216:     {
1217:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1218:       return -ENOLINK;
1219:     }
1220: 
1221:   if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY && g_active.quarantine)
1222:     {
1223:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1224:       return -ENOLINK;
1225:     }
1226: 
1227:   memset(&channel->pending, 0, sizeof(channel->pending));
1228:   memcpy(&channel->pending, message, sizeof(channel->pending));
1229:   channel->callback = callback;
1230:   channel->arg = arg;
1231:   channel->result = -EINPROGRESS;
1232:   channel->queued = true;
1233: 
1234:   if (up_cpu_index() == 0)
1235:     {
1236:       (void)dispatch_locked();
1237:     }
1238: 
1239:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1240: 
1241:   /* CPU1 callers only enqueue work.  Physical descriptors to the CP still
1242:    * originate exclusively from logical CPU0.
1243:    */
1244: 
1245:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
1246:   return OK;
1247: }

1264: int bk7258_mailbox_start_probe(void)
1265: {
1266:   irqstate_t flags;
1267: 
1268:   if (!g_initialized)
1269:     {
1270:       return -EAGAIN;
1271:     }
1272: 
1273:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1274:   if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN)
1275:     {
1276:       select_recovery_epoch();
1277:     }
1278:   /* A probe request is idempotent once the transport is ready.  The boot
1279:    * wait loop and the UART worker can request a probe concurrently; reopening
1280:    * a READY link here would abort a valid state ACK and race the first PWC
1281:    * transaction. */
1282: 
1283:   if (up_cpu_index() == 0)
1284:     {
1285:       (void)dispatch_locked();
1286:     }
1287: 
1288:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1289:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
1290:   return OK;
1291: }

151: void bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_poll(void)
152: {
153:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
154:   volatile uint32_t *payload =
155:     (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
156:   clock_t now;
157:   int ret;
158: 
159:   if (!g_heartbeat_enabled || g_heartbeat_pending)
160:     {
161:       return;
162:     }
163: 
164:   if (g_heartbeat_completions != g_heartbeat_reported)
165:     {
166:       g_heartbeat_reported = g_heartbeat_completions;
167:       if (g_heartbeat_reported <= 3u)
168:         {
169:           printf("IPC: heartbeat ACK result=%d count=%lu\n",
170:                  g_heartbeat_result,
171:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_reported);
172:         }
173:     }
174: 
175:   if (g_heartbeat_result < 0)
176:     {
177:       g_heartbeat_failures++;
178:       if ((g_heartbeat_failures & (g_heartbeat_failures - 1u)) == 0)
179:         {
180:           syslog(LOG_ERR, "IPC heartbeat failed: %d count=%lu\n",
181:                  g_heartbeat_result,
182:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_failures);
183:         }

186:     }

189:   if ((sclock_t)(now - g_next_heartbeat) < 0)

191:       return;
192:     }

194:   *payload = 0;
195:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
196:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
197:   message.header = IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION;
198:   message.payload_address = BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
199:   message.payload_length = sizeof(*payload);
200:   g_heartbeat_result = -EINPROGRESS;
201:   g_heartbeat_pending = true;
202:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX, &message,
203:                                  ipc_heartbeat_complete, NULL);
204:   if (ret == OK)
205:     {
206:       g_heartbeat_submissions++;
207:       g_next_heartbeat = now + IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL;
208:       if (g_heartbeat_submissions <= 3u)
209:         {
210:           printf("IPC: heartbeat queued count=%lu tick=%llu\n",
211:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_submissions,
212:                  (unsigned long long)now);
213:         }
214:     }
215:   else
216:     {
217:       g_heartbeat_pending = false;
218:       g_heartbeat_result = ret;
219:       g_next_heartbeat = now + IPC_HEARTBEAT_RETRY;
220:     }

21: #define MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT      (2u * 3u + 1u)
22: #define MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET   8u
23: 
24: struct mbox_rx_descriptor
25: {
26:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
27:   uint32_t order;
28:   bool used;
29: };
30: 
31: static bk7258_mbox_callback_t g_callback;
32: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor g_rx_desc[MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT];

39: static void mbox_trace_errors(void)
40: {
41:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(4,
42:     (g_stats.bad_source & 0xffu) |
43:     ((g_stats.bad_length & 0xffu) << 8) |
44:     ((g_stats.bad_address & 0xffu) << 16) |
45:     ((g_stats.descriptor_full & 0xffu) << 24));
46: }
47: 
48: _Static_assert(MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT > 2u * 3u,
49:                "RX descriptors must hold a deferred command and two FIFOs");
50: 
51: uint32_t bk7258_mbox_rx_status(void)
52: {
53:   return getreg32(up_cpu_index() == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
54:                                        BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS);
55: }
56: 
57: static void mbox_clear_errors(int cpu)
58: {
59:   uintptr_t cfg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG;
60:   uint32_t config = getreg32(cfg);
61:   uint32_t errors = config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_ERROR_STATUS;
62: 
63:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS) != 0)
64:     {
65:       g_stats.write_error++;
66:     }
67: 
68:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS) != 0)
69:     {
70:       g_stats.read_error++;
71:     }
72: 
73:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS) != 0)
74:     {
75:       g_stats.write_full++;
76:     }
77: 
78:   if (errors != 0)
79:     {
80:       putreg32((config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK) | errors, cfg);
81:     }
82: }

84: static bool mbox_valid_envelope(uint8_t source, uint32_t address,
85:                                 uint32_t length)
86: {
87:   if (source != 0)
88:     {
89:       g_stats.bad_source++;
90:       mbox_trace_errors();
91:       return false;
92:     }
93: 
94:   if (length != BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
95:     {
96:       g_stats.bad_length++;
97:       mbox_trace_errors();
98:       return false;
99:     }
100: 
101:   if ((address & 3u) != 0 || address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START ||
102:       address > BK7258_CP_RAM_END - BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
103:     {
104:       g_stats.bad_address++;
105:       mbox_trace_errors();
106:       return false;
107:     }
108: 
109:   return true;
110: }

112: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
113: {
114:   irqstate_t flags;
115:   uintptr_t status;
116:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
117: 
118:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
119:     {
120:       return -EINVAL;
121:     }
122: 
123: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
124:   if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
125:     {
126:       return -EPERM;
127:     }
128: #endif
129: 
130:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
131:    * receive FIFO status register.
132:    */
133: 
134:   status = destination == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
135:             destination == 1 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
136:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
137:   flags = up_irq_save();
138:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
139:     {
140:       up_irq_restore(flags);
141:       return -EAGAIN;
142:     }
143: 
144:   /* TDATA0/TDATA1 are staging registers and TID commits the descriptor.
145:    * Keep raw SMP kicks and transport sends from interleaving these writes.
146:    */
147: 
148:   putreg32(data[0], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA0 :
149:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA0);
150:   putreg32(data[1], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA1 :
151:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA1);
152:   putreg32(destination, cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TID :
153:                                    BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TID);
154:   up_irq_restore(flags);
155:   return OK;
156: }

158: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_alloc_desc(void)
159: {
160:   unsigned int i;
161: 
162:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
163:     {
164:       if (!g_rx_desc[i].used)
165:         {
166:           return &g_rx_desc[i];
167:         }
168:     }
169: 
170:   return NULL;
171: }

173: static bool mbox_priority_message(
174:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
175: {
176:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
177: 
178:   return (control & (BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0;
179: }
180: 
181: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_oldest_desc(bool priority)
182: {
183:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *oldest = NULL;
184:   unsigned int i;
185: 
186:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
187:     {
188:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc = &g_rx_desc[i];
189: 
190:       if (!desc->used || mbox_priority_message(&desc->message) != priority)
191:         {
192:           continue;
193:         }
194: 
195:       if (oldest == NULL || (int32_t)(desc->order - oldest->order) < 0)
196:         {
197:           oldest = desc;
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:   return oldest;
202: }
203: 
204: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
205: {
206:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
210:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
211:    */
212: 
213:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
214:     {
215:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
216:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
217:       g_processing_order = 0;
218:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
219:         {
220:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
221:           break;
222:         }
223: 
224:       desc->used = false;
225:     }
226: 
227:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
228:     {
229:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
230:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
231:       g_processing_order = 0;
232:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
233:         {
234:           break;
235:         }
236: 
237:       desc->used = false;
238:     }
239: }

241: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
242: {
243:   uintptr_t rdata0;
244:   uintptr_t rdata1;
245:   uintptr_t sidreg;
246:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
247:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
248: 
249:   (void)irq;
250:   (void)context;
251:   (void)arg;
252: 
253:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
254:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
255:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
256:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
257:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
258:     {
259:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
260:     }
261:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
262:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
263:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
264: 
265:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
266:     {
267:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
268:       uint32_t address;
269:       uint32_t length;
270:       uint8_t source;
271: 
272:       if (cpu == 0)
273:         {
274:           mbox_process_desc();
275:         }
276: 
277:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
278:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
279:         {
280:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
281:           mbox_trace_errors();
282:           break;
283:         }
284: 
285:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
286:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
287:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
288: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
289:       if (length == 0)
290:         {
291:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
292:             {
293:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
294:                 {
295:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
296:                 }
297: 
298:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
299:             }
300:           else
301:             {
302:               if (cpu == 0)
303:                 {
304:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
305:                   mbox_trace_errors();
306:                 }
307:             }
308: 
309:           continue;
310:         }
311: #endif
312: 
313:       if (cpu != 0)
314:         {
315:           continue;
316:         }
317: 
318:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
319:         {
320:           continue;
321:         }
322: 
323:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
324:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
325:              sizeof(desc->message));
326:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
327:       desc->used = true;
328:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
329:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
330:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
331:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
332:       mbox_process_desc();
333:     }
334: 
335:   if (cpu == 0)
336:     {
337:       mbox_process_desc();
338:     }
339: 
340:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
341:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
342:     {
343:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
344:     }
345: 
346:   return OK;
347: }

391: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)
392: {
393:   int ret;
394: 
395:   if (g_mbox_ready)
396:     {
397:       return OK;
398:     }
399: 
400:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));
401:   g_rx_order = 0;
402:   g_processing_order = 0;

405:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and
406:    * descriptors before enabling the route; pre-existing FIFO entries are

410:   putreg32(2u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
411:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
412:             BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG);
413:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG);
414: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
415:   putreg32(5u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
416:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
417:             BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG);
418:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH2_FIFO_CFG);
419: #endif
420:   modifyreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CTRL, 0, 1u << 2);

423:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_irq, NULL);

429:   g_mbox_ready = true;
430: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
431:   g_mbox_smp_ready = true;
432: #endif
433:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);

114: static int ipc_heartbeat_timeout(void)

116: 	u32   cur_time;
117: 
118: 	cur_time = (u32)rtos_get_time();
119: 
120: 	if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
121: 	{
122: 		return 0;
123: 	}
124: 	if((cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING) || (cpu_x_dump != 0))
125: 	{

127: 		return 0;
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	if(cur_time >= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)
131: 	{
132: 		cur_time -= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp;
133: 	}
134: 	else
135: 	{
136: 		cur_time += (~(cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)) + 1;  // wrap around.
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	if(cur_time < HB_TIMEOUT_MS)
140: 	{
141: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
142: 		return 0;
143: 	}
144: 
145: 	if (bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_get(PM_DEV_ID_DEFAULT))
146: 	{
147: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
148: 		bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_clear(PM_DEV_ID_DEFAULT);
149: 		return 0;
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	if(s_mb_ipc_work_state == MB_IPC_EXIT_LV)
153: 	{
154: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
155: 		s_mb_ipc_work_state = MB_IPC_WORKING;
156: 		return 0;
157: 	}
158: 
159: 	return 1;

237: 	{

239: 
240: 		if(events == 0)

242: 			// timeout, so check heartbeat.
243: 			events = MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG;
244: 		}
245: 
246: 		if(events & MB_IPC_STOP_CORE_FLAG)  // process this event at first!!!!
247: 		{
248: 			if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
249: 			{
250: 				events = 0;  // clear all events.
251: 			}
252: 		}
253: 
254: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)
255: 		{
256: 			u8   retry_cnt = 0;
257: 
258: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
259: 			{
260: 				ipc_heartbeat_timeout();
261: 
262: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)
263: 				{
264: 					if(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
265: 					{
266: 						cpu_x_state = CORE_POWER_ON;
267: 						break;  // cpu1 power on.
268: 					}
269: 				}
270: 				else
271: 				{
272: 					if( retry_cnt > 3)
273: 					{
274: 						BK_DUMP_OUT("IPC retry to start core%d, retry_cnt:%d\r\n", cpu_x_id, retry_cnt);
275: 						bk_pm_openvela_mailbox_diag_dump();
276: 						// restart_cpu_x();
277: 						break;
278: 					}
279: 					else
280: 					{
281: 						events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG, true, 2000);//2s
282: 					}
283: 				}
284: 
285: 				retry_cnt++;
286: 			}
287: 
288: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
289: 		}
290: 
291: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
292: 		{
293: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())
294: 			{
295: 				BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC[%d]heartbeat timeout %d,%d\r\n",cpu_x_id,cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp,(u32)rtos_get_time());

299: 				BK_ASSERT(false);
300: 			}
301: 		}
302: 
303: 		if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)

306: 		}
307: 		else
308: 		{

310: 		}
311: 	}

There are no standalone runtime `.log` files in the workspace. The runtime evidence is recorded in:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md`

The relevant tested configuration appears to be the SMP configuration in:

## Overall conclusion

The historical failure absolutely was caused by a higher-priority CP boot task starving the lower-priority CP mailbox/UART bridge task. That specific issue is fixed in the current CP source by directly polling the mailbox during the CPU1 boot transaction and delaying for 1 ms on every iteration.

The current AP startup waits also explicitly drain mailbox RX, so the current link, HW_CTRL, and PWC waits do not depend solely on a lower-priority worker consuming IRQ-delivered ACKs.

However, there are still concrete scheduling and locking defects:

1. The AP transport TX and UART workers remain below several CPU0-bound workers until very late in bring-up.
2. The AP Wi-Fi worker has an unbounded high-priority drain loop and can starve the transport workers under continuous input.
3. The motor worker bypasses the PWC serialization mutex and can race the PWC worker on the single PWC logical channel.
4. The CP runtime bridge still couples mailbox polling to console processing and unbounded bridge work. The startup path compensates for this, but normal runtime polling can still be delayed.
5. The current source relies on callbacks being safe while the mailbox recursive spinlock is held. This is currently mostly safe, but it remains a fragile lock contract.

---

## 1. Historical CP bridge starvation: confirmed, now mitigated

### Historical bug

The original CP CPU1 boot loop was a pure busy poll:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:347-358`

It repeatedly read the AON RTC without yielding and did not call `mb_chnl_poll()`.

The checked-in test history identifies the consequence explicitly:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:464-473`

The log diagnosis was:

- CP CPU1 boot code waited in a high-priority 10-second loop.
- The loop starved the only task running `bk_mb_uart_poll()`, namely `ap_console`.
- CP hardware received the AP descriptor, but the logical UART STATE ACK was not dispatched.

This is a real priority starvation bug, not an AP mailbox transmission failure.

### Current state

The current CP implementation now does:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhineng/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:682-691`

```c
mb_chnl_poll();
current_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(...);
rtos_delay_milliseconds(1);
```

This directly drains the mailbox while the high-priority boot task is active and yields to lower-priority tasks.

The CP mailbox channel layer also serializes concurrent polling:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhineng/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:1157-1175`

`ap_console` still polls through:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhineng/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:210-232`

### Minimal change

No additional startup change is required for this historical bug as long as the current direct polling and 1 ms delay remain.

For additional runtime robustness, the minimal architectural change would be:

- move `mb_chnl_poll()` into a dedicated bounded mailbox task, or
- ensure every high-priority CP transaction loop continues to call `mb_chnl_poll()` and yields.

Do not revert to a pure AON-RTC busy loop.

---

## 2. Current AP priority inversion: transport workers are activated too late

### Priority layout

The AP priorities are:

- Bring-up thread: `100`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhineng/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:22-24`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhineng/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:188-203`
- Mailbox TX worker during boot: `95`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:37-38`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1118-1128`
- Mailbox TX worker after activation: `105`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1151-1157`
- Mailbox UART worker during boot: `95`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:40-41`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:550-570`
- Mailbox UART worker after activation: `106`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:575-585`
- PWC worker: `110`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:479`
- AP heartbeat worker: `110`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:28`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:251-254`
- Wi-Fi worker: `110`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1951`

All these AP workers are pinned to logical CPU0, either explicitly or through affinity inheritance:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:200-203`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1096-1104`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:97-107`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_ipc_heartbeat.c:43-53`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:76-86`

### Problem

The transport workers are not raised to their operational priorities until the very end of bring-up:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:127-143`

They remain at priority 95 while the following work runs:

- HW_CTRL startup
- PWC worker startup
- PSRAM power and initialization
- OpenVela ready handshake
- Wi-Fi initialization
- power-key motor worker startup

Synchronous startup waits are protected by direct mailbox draining, so this ordering does not explain the already-fixed UART-link or PWC-ACK failures by itself. Nevertheless, it creates a real dependency hazard for any asynchronous transaction issued during those phases. A CPU0 task at priority 100 or 110 can prevent the lower-priority transport workers from running.

### Minimal change

Move:

```c
bk7258_mailbox_workers_activate();
bk7258_mb_uart_worker_activate();
```

from the end of `bk7258_bringup()` to immediately after both workers are created, or at least before starting Wi-Fi and other asynchronous services.

The direct RX drain should remain in the synchronous waits even after this change.

## 3. Current AP Wi-Fi worker can starve mailbox TX/UART workers

This is the clearest remaining AP scheduling bug.

### Evidence

The Wi-Fi worker is priority 110:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1951`

Its outer loop waits on a semaphore, but once awakened it has an unbounded inner drain loop:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1407-1461`

```c
for (;;)
  {
    ...
    for (;;)
      {
        ...
        if (g_wifi.node_count == 0)
          break;

        ...
        wifi_handle_command_list(...);
        ...
        wifi_handle_data(...);

        bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
      }
  }
```

There is no bounded batch count and no explicit yield inside the inner loop.

The mailbox TX worker is only priority 105 after activation, and the UART worker is 106:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:37-38`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:40-41`

Because all are CPU0-bound, continuous CP Wi-Fi traffic can keep `g_wifi.node_count` nonzero and prevent `mbox-v2` and `mb-uart0` from running. This can cause:

- transport transactions to remain logically queued or active;
- UART TX progress to stall;
- heartbeat or PWC asynchronous messages to be delayed;
- apparent mailbox ACK timeouts even though physical RX polling is occurring.

`bk7258_mbox_kick_rx()` inside the Wi-Fi loop helps consume RX descriptors, but it does not guarantee that the lower-priority TX worker will run.

### Minimal change

Use either of these minimal fixes:

1. Bound the Wi-Fi work per iteration, for example process a fixed number of nodes and then yield with `nxsig_usleep(0)` or equivalent; or
2. Lower the Wi-Fi worker below the transport workers, for example below priority 105/106.

The safer change is a bounded batch plus yield. Lowering the Wi-Fi priority alone may increase latency but is simpler.

The same review should be applied to any future high-priority worker that drains a queue in an unbounded loop.

## 4. PWC worker priority is unnecessarily above the transport workers

The PWC worker runs at priority 110:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:479`

It normally blocks on `g_pwc_sem`, so it does not continuously starve lower-priority tasks during idle periods. However, it can process a stream of queued CP notifications without an explicit yield:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:349-445`

Some cases also perform a synchronous PWC send and wait from the same worker:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:396-407`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:421-438`

Those waits do block, so they do not permanently monopolize CPU0. The risk is the unbounded sequence of nonblocking queue items or diagnostic commands.

### Minimal change

Either:

- lower PWC worker priority below mailbox TX/UART, while keeping it above the priority of the bring-up thread; or
- process a bounded number of PWC queue entries before yielding.

A reasonable ordering is:

```text
mailbox UART worker   > mailbox TX worker > PWC/Wi-Fi worker > bring-up/application
```

For example, PWC/Wi-Fi at 104, mailbox TX at 105, and UART at 106 would preserve transport progress while still allowing PWC startup to run ahead of the priority-100 bring-up thread.

This should be validated against expected PWC response latency before changing the numeric values.

## 5. Motor worker bypasses PWC transaction serialization

### Evidence

PWC synchronous sends are serialized by `g_pwc_tx_lock`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:55`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:164-190`

The motor worker does not use that helper. It directly performs:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:78-87`

```c
bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(...);
bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(200);
```

The motor worker is created at priority 100:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:187-206`

The PWC worker is priority 110 and can independently call `pwc_send_wait()` in response to CP requests. Both use the same single logical channel:

- `BK7258_MB_CHAN_PWC_TX`

The mailbox transport allows only one queued transaction per logical channel:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1203-1210`

Therefore the motor request can race a PWC worker response and receive `-EBUSY`. The motor path exits on that error, so this is not an ACK-consumption deadlock, but it is a concrete cross-worker transaction failure.

### Minimal change

Make the motor request use the same serialized PWC send/wait helper as the PWC worker.

Minimal options:

- expose a common `bk7258_pwc_send_wait()` API and use it from `bk7258_motor.c`; or
- add a mutex around the motor’s send-and-wait sequence shared with `bk7258_pm_pwc.c`; or
- defer motor startup until the PWC startup transaction is completely finished and ensure all later PWC requests still use one serializer.

The first option is the cleanest and smallest behavioral change.

## 6. CP bridge polling remains coupled to potentially lengthy console work

### Evidence

The CP bridge task performs all of the following in one loop:

- waits on its semaphore;
- calls `bk_mb_uart_poll()`;
- drains UART RX;
- forwards logs;
- performs retry delays;
- drains the complete AP-to-CP TX bridge ring.

Relevant code:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:210-232`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:243-311`

`ap_bridge_log_output()` can perform up to three retries with a 10 ms delay:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:134-156`

`ap_bridge_drain_tx()` loops until the bridge ring or mailbox UART space is empty:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:165-207`

Thus mailbox polling can be delayed by console formatting, log-queue retries, or a long TX drain. During startup, the CP power-control task compensates by directly calling `mb_chnl_poll()`. During normal runtime, mailbox polling still depends on the `ap_console` task.

### Minimal change

Separate mailbox polling from console presentation:

- add a dedicated bounded mailbox poll task; or
- call `mb_chnl_poll()` from a short, high-priority mailbox service before doing log formatting/TX draining.

At minimum, bound `ap_bridge_drain_tx()` and avoid sleeping in the same task that owns mailbox polling.

This is a latency/starvation issue, not the original startup deadlock, because the current startup path directly polls.

## 7. Current lock use: recursive driver lock is intentional, but the callback contract is fragile

### Current behavior

The mailbox RX path acquires `g_bk7258_driver_lock` and invokes logical callbacks while holding it:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:866-908`

`complete_transaction()` also invokes TX completion callbacks while holding the same lock:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:330-353`

Several callbacks reacquire that lock:

- UART completion:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:170-254`
- Wi-Fi completions:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:249-280`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:945-968`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1076-1098`

This works because `g_bk7258_driver_lock` is an `rspinlock_t`, and the current SMP configuration enables recursive ownership:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:666-704`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:1035-1063`

The PWC RX callback was specifically changed not to recursively acquire the lock:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:314-331`

The README confirms the former PWC recursive-lock problem:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:589-595`

### Assessment

There is no current unconditional recursive-lock deadlock in this path. The lock is recursive by design.

The concrete remaining risk is that callbacks execute arbitrary code while:

- interrupts are disabled;
- the global driver spinlock is held;
- scheduling is suppressed.

That makes callback execution time part of the mailbox critical section. A future callback that waits on a semaphore, takes a mutex, or invokes a non-recursive lock can deadlock the mailbox IRQ path.

### Minimal change

Do not perform blocking operations from mailbox callbacks. For a stronger fix:

- copy completion state under `g_bk7258_driver_lock`;
- release the lock;
- invoke the callback afterward.

That is more invasive, so the minimal immediate change is to document/enforce that all mailbox callbacks are nonblocking and only enqueue work.

### HW_CTRL and PWC waits

The common channel wait also explicitly drains RX:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1419-1457`

This is used by:

- HW_CTRL:

Therefore, the current startup wait is not blocked merely because `mbox-v2` or `mb-uart0` is at priority 95. The waiting bring-up/PWC/HW_CTRL context itself calls `bk7258_mbox_kick_rx()`.

## Recommended minimal change set

1. **Keep the current CP fix**
   - Retain `mb_chnl_poll()` plus `rtos_delay_milliseconds(1)` in the CPU1 boot loop.
   - Do not restore the original busy AON-RTC-only loop.

2. **Activate AP transport workers earlier**
   - Move `bk7258_mailbox_workers_activate()` and `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_activate()` to immediately after worker creation, or at least before Wi-Fi and other asynchronous services start.

3. **Bound the AP Wi-Fi worker**
   - Add a per-pass work limit and yield in the inner queue-draining loop at:
     - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1419-1461`
   - Alternatively lower its priority below mailbox TX/UART.

4. **Serialize all PWC-channel users**
   - Route the motor worker through the same PWC send/wait mutex used by:
     - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:164-190`
   - The direct motor path at:
     - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:78-87`
     should not remain unsynchronized.

5. **Decouple CP mailbox polling from console formatting**
   - Prefer a dedicated bounded mailbox poll task.
   - At minimum, bound `ap_bridge_drain_tx()` and avoid long log retry work in the same task that performs `bk_mb_uart_poll()`.

6. **Preserve current CPU0 sequencing**
   - Keep CPU2 scheduler readiness polling before affinity changes and worker creation.
   - Keep `bk7258_timer_start()` after CPU0 affinity is guaranteed:
     - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1090-1110`

## Bottom line

- **Historical CP starvation:** real and confirmed; current direct polling plus 1 ms delay fixes it.
- **Current startup ACK consumption:** explicit RX draining means startup does not inherently wait with ACKs unable to be consumed.
- **Current AP scheduling risk:** real; the priority-110 Wi-Fi/PWC consumers can starve priority-105/106 transport workers on CPU0, especially Wi-Fi’s unbounded queue drain.
- **Current locking bug:** the motor PWC path bypasses the PWC mutex and can collide on the single logical PWC channel.
- **Current CP bridge design risk:** mailbox polling remains coupled to lower-priority console work outside the startup loop, so runtime transport latency can still be unbounded under higher-priority CP load.
